text.p: Sudan's Finance Minister Abdel Wahab Osman said in the 1997 budget that inflation would fall to 70 percent from 160 percent and forecasts a deficit of 251 billion pounds ($172.6 million).
Osman made his remarks to parliament late on Monday in a draft budget speech that was broadcast by Sudanese television.
The cabinet has already approved the budget.
The minister said total expenditure was forecast at 1,306 billion Sudanese pounds against revenues of 1,055 billion pounds.
Local financing would cover 87 billion pounds of the deficit while foreign finance would account for 61 billion, Osman added.
The remaining deficit, 103 billion pounds, would be covered by the banking system, he said.
The minister said oil and gold would form, for the first time, a source of revenue.
Earlier this year, Sudan said it had started commercial production of oil in the central state of Kordofan. A Sudanese French joint venture has been mining gold near the Red Sea since 1991.
Osman said oil would account for 3.6 percent of total revenue and gold 2.4 percent.
